correctness.rationale: For n>=17, all six published alternative linear upper bounds have positive and increasing gaps below 1+binom(n,2), forcing either a pure weight-two layer or a common-two-core graph with three disjoint external edges. In the latter case both bounds of Lemma 6.1 must saturate. The pure weight-two deficit identity rules out isolated supports, and the forbidden odd distances impose unique common symbols, first on all outer pairs and then on each spoke and the core word. Center uniqueness follows because every noncenter pair-flip word is at distance four from some disjoint pair-flip word. The exact count follows by injectively choosing q^n centers and (q-1)^n alternates. Finite code verifies construction/injectivity on sample regimes and independently checks case gaps; preprint estimates are explicitly an imported premise.

value.rationale: A maximum-size theorem by itself does not settle all equality configurations. The result determines the entire unrestricted ternary and quaternary extremizer structure, identifies one Hamming-isometry class, a unique center and exact labeled counts (q(q-1))^n across an unbounded natural range n>=17. Its proof genuinely exploits equality in multiple support-layer bounds and synchronized letter values, not a routine substitution or known cardinality table.
